fields.Name: Antifungal Hydrosol Blend
fields.Purpose: Make an Antifungal Hydrosol Spray blend
fields.Notes:
Note on shelf life: This blend is water-based (hydrosol) and doesn't contain any preservatives, so you'll want to make a fresh bottle every few weeks. Be sure to read the All About Preservatives and Antioxidants reference page.

 

* Solubol: As you know, essential oils and water do not mix. When essential oils are added into a water or hydrosol spray, the tiny droplets of essential oil stay separate from the water/hydrosol. When sprayed on the body we get tiny droplets of neat essential oil on our skin. To evenly disperse essential oil into the water/hydrosol we use "Solubol.” It works great to protect the skin from neat essential oil and has a very mild aroma that doesn't seem to influence the aroma of the blend. We use Solubol in sprays we make for damaged or sensitive skin, not for the average spray blend.

There is some debate about how much Solubol one needs to fully disperse essential oil into the water. The range seems to go from 1:1 ratio (1 drop Solubol to 1 drop essential oil), to 1:8 (8 drops Solubol to 1 drop essential oil). The folks we buy it from use it at a 1:4 ratio (1 drop essential oil to 4 drops Solubol). Aromatics International's Solubol is made in France. It has a 2-year shelf life.

It is an all-natural product, here are the ingredients:

Sucrose Stearate – An emulsifier made from sugar and vegetable oil
Helianthus annus – Annual sunflower oil
Cera alba – Beeswax
Sterculia urens – a medium-sized, deciduous tree that exudes a gum called karaya used in food as an emulsifier, stabilizer, and thickener
The gum of the acacia tree
Propolis Wax from bees
fields.Directions:
Choose 4–5 essential oils for this blend.

Step 1: Search the Component Database for two variables: antifungal and monoterpenols. Go to search on the left-hand navigation, choose antifungal from the therapeutic property list on the right, and monoterpenol for the chemical family on the left, then click the red search button.

Step 2: Read all the component datasheets that your search results show.

Step 3: Search on Aromatics International for the oils high those components from your search

Step 4: Choose 4–5 oils for your antifungal spray. Use a total of approximately 30 drops of essential oil in the 2 oz spray (3% dilution).

Step 5: Add 4 drops of Solubol* for each drop of essential oil used. If you use 30 drops of essential oils, how much solubol? Yup, 120 drops. I know, it is a lot, but that is what it takes for the solubol to blend the essential oil into the water. If you have a small graduated cylinder that measures by the ml (milliliter) use that and add 6 ml, rather than counting 120 drops! (There are about 20 drops per ml.)

Step 6: Make your label. You can create a name for the blend, or put the ingredients on the label, or both.

Helichrysum italicum ssp. serotinum (helichrysum) essential oil
In a 10 milliliter bottle, blend 10 drops each of palmarosa and helichrysum essential oil with St. John’s wort (Hypericum perforatum) macerated oil. Apply twice a day on the breast until the pain diminishes.
fields.Directions:
4 milliliters Ocimum basilicum ssp. basilicum (tropical basil) essential oil – A major antispasmodic with immediate effects
3 milliliters Cananga odorata (ylang-ylang) essential oil – Antispasmodic, analgesic, relaxing to the nervous system.
2.5 milliliters Chamaemelum nobilis (Roman chamomile) essential oil – Analgesic, calming to the mind, relaxes emotional tension
Mix essential oils in a 15 milliliter bottle. Fill with hazelnut or apricot kernel oil.

Application: Massage the pelvic area gently with 6 to 8 drops of the blend for 10 days before the period is due, 2 to 3 times per day. A warm compress with a couple of drops of each essential oil applied on the pelvic region can be very comforting during painful cramps. If the person is stressed, rub 3 drops of the blend on the solar plexus.

fields.Name: Hand Gel (Monoterpenol high)
fields.Purpose: A hand gel to keep your hands feeling cool, refreshed, and silky smooth!
fields.Directions:
Step 1: This is an easy blend! Review the datasheets for the oils high in monoterpenols and find the ones that are skin-nourishing and cleansing. Consider the oils that would be nourishing to the skin and also cleansing. Hint: Palmarosa is one.

Step 2: I like to use a 3% dilution for hand sanitizers. So…here we go…2 oz carrier, 3% dilution…how many drops?

You got it! 30–36 (3% is 15–18 drops, times 2) If for any reason you are not familiar with these blending guidelines, check out the Learn More section at Aromatics International.

Step 3: Here are a few blending hints: Gingergrass and Ghandi Root are beautiful together. Palmarosa and Coriander make a lovely combination.

Step 4: Use the drop-by-drop blending technique to make this blend, right into the 2 oz of aloe vera gel. Remember to save all your recipes.

Step 5: Make your label.

This blend is in aloe vera gel (water-based carrier) and is not preserved, so be sure you have read the All About Preservatives and Antioxidants reference page.

Note on Solubol: When using Aloe Vera Gel that has xanthan gum as a thickening agent, it can give some dispersion between the water-based aloe vera and the essential oils. However, it won't disperse 100% and the blend does need to be shaken before each use.  This is why you might want to consider adding  4 ml of solubol to this recipe.

Note on Hand Gel: The hand gels we share are not sanitizers—they contain essential oils and aloe vera gel, and no alcohol. The Aromahead Approach is to make blends as natural as possible. We use our hand gel for normal everyday use and recommend thorough handwashing with soap and water for the tough stuff!

Summary: This is a great blend for travel, or just to carry around in your bag, backpack, and car!

fields.Name: Whipped Shea and Kombo Butter
fields.Purpose: Did we mention this body butter has a rich, velvety aroma that is simply divine? If you love body butter, this one is a must-try! Due to the Kombo butter, this blend is perfect for those who have areas of pain and inflammation as well. It is multi-purpose!
fields.Notes:
4 oz. Shea Butter
2 oz. Cocoa Butter
2 oz. Kombo Butter
1 oz Jojoba
Melt the shea and cocoa butters in a double boiler.
Once melted, take off of the heat and add the Kombo Butter and jojoba.
Once all the butters are incorporated, place in the refrigerator until cool and the top begins to harden slightly.
Blend with a mixer on high speed for 3 - 4 minutes, resting for two minutes. Continue this for approximately 20-30 minutes until you obtain a gorgeous whipped butter!
Once whipped, feel free to add essential oils of choice.
